primitives.verbatim_quote: The nerve-centres are so organized that certain stimuli pull the trigger of certain explosive parts ; and a creature going through one of these explosions for the first time undergoes an entirely novel experience.

primitives.breakdown_regime: First-time exposure to novel stimulus leads to unpredictable behavioral output.

primitives.name: Volitional Learning Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: When a particular movement, having once occurred in a random, reflex, or involuntary way, has left an image of itself in the memory, then the movement can be desired again, proposed as an end, and deliberately willed.
primitives.assumptions: Memory encodes past involuntary events enabling future intentional reproduction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Absence of prior involuntary experience precludes volitional control.

layer2.mapping: Volitional learning mirrors reinforcement learning feedback loops between sensory input and motor output.
layer2.telemetry: Repetition rate of desired movement after initial involuntary occurrence

primitives.breakdown_regime: First-time volition impossible without prior knowledge of action's consequences.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core thesis posits that volition arises not from direct conscious choice but from a hierarchical process: involuntary neural explosions form the basis of all behavior, which are then encoded into memory. Subsequent volitional acts are derived from these stored patterns. This implies a duality between automaticity and deliberation—whereby the former provides the raw material for the latter. In GSI, this manifests as a Bayesian framework where prior beliefs about motoric capabilities are updated based on observed involuntary responses. The GSE interprets this as a Markovian state transition system, where each involuntary reaction becomes a node in a graph of possible future actions. The failure mode occurs when an agent lacks sufficient past involuntary experiences to build a reliable model of its own agency. Thus, the mathematical structure reflects both a temporal dependency and a recursive self-modeling mechanism.
